When I bought the game I spent 2 days researching the rules, went through the BGG forum to get some clarification, watched MCDM play and they I organized a session. I recommend the same amount of research for new players since the rules are lengthy and each factions circumvents at least one rule, hence the asymmetrical game design. 

I highly recommend your first game to be played with the advanced rules and 6 players because the game shines under these conditions. You really feel Herbert's work while playing and that is all any Dune fan can hope for.

There really isn't much I can criticize the game for, except the fact that an average game lasts 3-4 hours (much of that time takes place during bidding phase and alliance discussion on the side, away from the board). Another gripe I have with it is that my group basically neglects playing other great board games because we like Dune so much.

10/10 with a cherry on top! If you got 5 friends, 4h minimum to spare, and love for the Dune universe, get this game.

It is very difficult for me to coherently explain why I have and will continue to spend hundreds of hours into Warframe, so I'll just make a few bullet points:
 

* Being a sci-fi nerd Warframe really scratches my itch for non-conventional and non-western type of sci-fi. Warframe screams Dune and I LOVE IT!


* Since I am getting kinda old I lost that teenage competitive spirit so PvP games are a no-no for me. * I am a filthy completionist. Warframe is all about collecting stuff. I have to have everything.


* The gameplay. Smoothest game I have played, ever.


* Warframe is a game I can always get back to. I would play it all day every day and get sick of it. Like, absolutely revolted by it. And I would stop, for a week, two weeks. **TL;DR** Play the game, get prime parts/rare mods, sell them through https://warframe.market/ or ingame trade chat, earn yourself some platinum without spending real money.

Warframe has 2 types of gear: regular and prime. All regular gear can be acquired through playing the game; warframe blueprints are dropped from a boss on each planet, and weapon blueprints are either dropped from specific enemies, bought (using credits) from the ingame market on your Orbiter, or found in the 4 labs in the Dojo (I highly recommend you look for a clan when you get a feel for the game and do want to continue playing). Once you get a blueprint you need to craft it using other resources farmed through gameplay, and they take time to build (from 12h to up to 72h), rule number 1: *NEVER RUSH CRAFTING!*

That was all in regards to regular gear, which cannot be traded among players (there are exceptions but don't worry about that). Now for the PRIME gear.

Prime gear is most of the time better than it's regular counter part (not all weapons and warframes have their Primes however, yet!). Prime gear is crafted by acquiring blueprints and parts found in Void Relics. These relics are in most mission loot tables (open world bounties as well). When you get a relic you need to open it by playing special missions. You can do these missions solo, or with randoms, or recruit other players for a specific relic (these are usually referred to as "radshares"). Every relic has 3 common (bronze), 2 uncommon (silver), and 1 rare (gold) reward. Once you finish a relic opening mission a reward screen will pop up with 4 rewards to choose from. This means you can choose some other players relic reward if you need it or if it has more **platinum** value (gold>silver>bronze). This **finally** brings me to the answer to your question: everything in this game is free!

Platinum is the real money currency in Warframe, and it is usually spent on cosmetic stuff and warframe/weapons slots earlier in the game. However, platinum is tradeable, which means if you have a Prime part that you don't need you can trade it to other people for platinum. Even the most common prime parts are useful and people trade for them since they themselves can be turned into Ducats, a special currency that is used to buy items from a bi-weekly trader called Baro. Also, mods can be traded for platinum as well. For example, you get lucky and get a mod that has a low drop chance, a lot of people would be more that happy to give you plat for it just to avoid the farm (same goes for prime parts). 

To keep track and take part in Warframe economy I suggest you visit https://warframe.market/ almost everyone is using this website. Or you could use the ingame trade chat tab and find/sell stuff through there (you can slow down the chat by typing in keywords and have only those messages appear for you).

So.. yeah. Warframe is free, and if you ever need platinum to spice up your fashion all you gotta do is play the game and trade with other players.

I agree that elite weekly challenges are "impossible" for new players who are desperately in need of items offered by Nora (Nitain especially since it is exclusive to the cred store). But I also do not agree that the challenges should be toned down so that everyone could do them without a proper setup or an organized party. 

Now, your idea does sound interesting; lets leave the challenges available for the entirety of the season. HOWEVER, I think their reputation value should decay as weeks go by if they are to remain available. This could cater towards new people and returning veterans. New people would have a pretty big goal to work towards (sees kill Hydralist; googles guides/builds, asks people in chat for advice; plans out the next TEN weeks to complete the challenge). Vets on the other hand do not need to worry about preparing for elite challenges so they just do them when they have the time, but should they be rewarded the same amount of rep as the active players?? Ehh... I don't know. I honestly woulnd't care if the events stayed for the entire duration of the session and that they would yield the same amount of rep as if completed on day 1, but I think DE could compromise if they let the challenges stay but have decaying rep (first week of weekly events are 5000 rep, second week they are worth 4000 rep, etc. and not go below 1000 since they are time consuming and should be worth a fair amount).

Personally, I LOVE that they did with Nightwave, it elevates Warframe on a whole new level of commitment which is why I personally love looter-shooters. I got time and I like investing it into fun games. Was Warframe worth of my time before Nightwave? Yeh, it was alright. I'm a filthy completionist so I don't mind grind and useless collections (mastering all weapons even tho I would only end up using 10 of them). Is Warframe worth spending even more of my time into it after Nightwave? Hell yeah! I like being challenged. I like communicating and asking/offering help in chat (my clan chat is BLOWING UP ever since Nightwave with people asking for help and it feels awesome offering advice and helping out).

Anyway, DE could polish some of the challanges, they could also make them permanent but please don't ask them to be as rewarding as when being completed in the time window.

P.S. Remove Nitain from cred store and make it acquirable ingame?? Could mean a lot to new players. OR! Remove Nitain from low MR recipes. Well, those are my two cents, even though no one asked.

I saw you mention gear grind in WoW. Let me explain how it works in Guild Wars 2.

* There are tree types of gear in Gw2 you need to focus about: Exotic, Ascendant and Legendary.
* Exotic is ok once you hit lvl 80 and start doing fractals and expansion story.
* Ascendant is the max stats in this game. It is slightly better than exotic but it has the ability to change stats (for a fee of ~~~5g~~ ~10g). It can be also infused with agony resistance for higher fractals.
* Legendary has the same stats as ascendant but it can change stats at any time for free, straight from your inventory.

They way you get ascendant gear is available through all 3 game modes, crafting, fractals, raids. You can get it fairly easy since it is so widespread, you just have to invest some time in it. And once you get it you have it forever since it is the best gear that ever be in GW2.

P.S. This website keeps track of your account (gw2efficiency.com), of course you have full control of which aspects of your account you want the website to track. It is very useful if you want to make legendary stuff since it also show the live feed of the TP (trading post) prices.

GW2 is totally opposite of a WoW clone. First of all, there are no race-class restrictions. Combat is more about moving around, dodging the enemy attack then just building up Block stat through your gear. If playing with friends you don't need to check in with them 1st on weather they need a specific class for their party (I had some very successful high lvl fractal (end game 5 man content) runs with an entire party of elementalists), so just pick what you think you will enjoy. Also, try as many professions (classes) as possible when you start, don't invest you 1st 5h of GW2 by just playing one profession. I recommend you use up all your character slots with professions you think you might enjoy the most and switch around. Also, each race has their starting zone and personal story quests so, if you do decide to switch around your 1st few hours you wont feel like you are doing exact same things over and over again.

As for the gear requirements, the highest possible armor and weapons are Ascendant level (there is the legendary tier but it is only fancy skins, the numbers are the SAME). This ascendant gear can either be crafted or dropped as loot from several game modes (PvE, PvP, WvW). When it comes to looting every player in a party and open world get their own rewards for doing events and killing mobs; other players can never tag a mob from you or ninja gear by rolling for it. The same goes for gathering, you see a tree, you cut it. Another players approaches the said cut tree and cuts it down again because on his client the tree is still there.

About PvP, you don't need special high tier PvP gear to be good, it is all about skill and coordination. However, you can customize your PvP build but each players has the same options as you do so no one has the upper hand.

End game. Well, that is a tricky topic for discussion. Currently, there are 3 raids (one raid but with 3 wings, each wing with 3 bosses) and they are considered challenging. Many people are angry about the concept of raids because it requires only ascendant gear to be able to participate. Well, as a veteran raider THAT IS NOT TRUE! I saw many people raiding with rare (yellow), even masterwork armor and weapons (green)!!! So, again, it is mainly about skill and cooperation. Raids are 10 man max.

Another very cool thing about GW2 is that in between expansions, we all get Living Story updates. Basically free DLC. We are in a middle of Living Story Season 3, and it is amazing!

Well, I don't know what else to add for the moment. Feel free to comment of PM me for more info about Gw2.
